item.title: Rethinking Edge-Device Collaborative LLM Inference for 6G AI Edge: An Empirical Evaluation
item.description: arXiv:2611.27994v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: 6G ubiquitous intelligence requires generative AI capabilities that far exceed the compute, memory, and energy budgets of mobile terminals. By pushing large language model (LLM) inference to proximate network edge, 6G is shifting to the AI Edge era via four edge-device collaborative paradigms: edge inference, model routing, model split, and speculative decoding. However, existing evaluations are predominantly conducted in idealized datacenter settings, masking the practical challenges posed by heterogeneous hardware and stochastic wireless channels at 6G AI Edge. This article presents the first unified, hardware-in-the-loop empirical study that re-examines these paradigms under practical network conditions. Our stage-wise latency evaluation reveals that network dynamics can inflate Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) by up to 6x, while massive tensor transmissions delay speculative decoding by 246 ms and consume over 150 ms in model split. Because no single paradigm universally dominates across all performance dimensions, we advocate for a context-aware adaptive orchestration framework that dynamically selects collaboration strategies based on network conditions, terminal capabilities, and task semantics, and outline a research roadmap toward 6G AI Edge deployment.
item.dc:creator: Cheng Wu, Xinchen Lyu, Chenshan Ren, Ziyao Yan, Qimei Cui, Xiaofeng Tao, Yang Yang

item.title: Intelligence as a Founding Principle: The O-RAN Architecture for Artificial Intelligence and Its Reference Implementations
item.description: arXiv:2611.28282v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Since its inception, O-RAN has established openness and intelligence as founding principles of the RAN, transforming closed base stations into disaggregated, multi-vendor systems with a hierarchical RIC. This article traces AI/ML in O-RAN through open specifications and reference implementations to 6G design. We examine how open fronthaul, RIC interfaces, cloud orchestration, and AAL profiles support control loops across multiple timescales, model management, and hardware acceleration. Commercial deployments and OTIC testing demonstrate multi-vendor interoperability. Open-source stacks and testbeds support pre-standardization studies of in-node dApps. Within this architecture, GPU-based AI-RAN platforms realize the inline High-PHY split on shared RAN and AI compute, providing one reference implementation path for the O-RAN AAL alongside other implementations on heterogeneous hardware. Vector instruction sets and analog in-memory computing offer longer-term options for improving energy efficiency. For 6G, extending intelligence to time-critical radio processing and mobile agent services calls for deadline-bounded third-party inference, energy-efficient RAN/Edge-AI silicon co-design, and agent session continuity across handovers. We propose a RAC that coordinates agents across tiers through local shells and a shared exposure gateway, with in-node operating bounds delivered asynchronously. We also propose Recursive Standardization, in which results from federated open labs inform candidate 6G requirements and standards review guides the next round of implementation and testing.
item.dc:creator: Chih-Lin I, Hao Xu, Tao Chen

item.title: ImCDN: An Immersive Content Delivery Network for Cooperative Tile-level 360 Video Streaming
item.description: arXiv:2611.28473v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Delivering immersive 360 video over Content Distribution Networks (CDNs) demands ultra-high bitrates, yet each user's viewport covers only a small fraction of the full panorama. Therefore, conventional segment-level architectures waste scarce edge resources on unseen regions. This paper presents ImCDN, an immersive end-to-end tile-granularity CDN framework that integrates field-of-view (FoV)-driven cloud pre-distribution with hybrid segment-tile caching at edge servers, edge compute for on-demand tile transcoding, and an edge-to-edge relay mechanism for cooperative content sharing. We formulate the CDN optimization problem, comprising cache admission, compute scheduling, and serving-node selection, as a long-term utility maximization that balances cache hit-rate, edge sharing, end-to-end latency, backhaul traffic, energy consumption, viewport video quality, and cache replacement cost. We solve it via multi-agent proximal policy optimization (MAPPO) under centralized training and decentralized execution across edge servers. Simulations on a realistic topology with real 360 head-tracking traces show that ImCDN improves edge hit rate and reduces user waiting time, reduces origin traffic by approximately 18% compared to the non-cooperative edge variant, and outperforms segment-only CDN baselines at comparable immersive quality (e.g., 4K/6K) and standard caching heuristics.
item.dc:creator: Ning Wang, Xiaofan Liu, Beatriz Lorenzo, Sumudu Samarakoon

item.title: Covertness Recovery in Multi-RAT UAV Swarms Under Post-Detection Threat Escalation via Lifelong Reinforcement Learning
item.description: arXiv:2611.28486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarms increasingly span multiple spectrum bands and radio access technologies (RATs), e.g., Wi-Fi, LoRa, Zigbee, and cellular. With active adversaries capable of protocol-aware jamming, spoofing, traffic analysis, and control-plane exploitation, survivable and timely covert communication is challenging. Moreover, after detection, adversaries may escalate with selective, adaptive attacks that increase latency and hinder recovery. This paper is the first to study covertness recovery under post-detection threat escalation. We design a learning-based mechanism that re-establishes covert communication across learning domains with different Willie densities and attack models, amid stochastic task arrivals, UAV mobility, and uncertain warden locations and behaviors. We jointly optimize RAT selection, resource allocation, and task offloading to minimize Age of Covert Information (AoCI), energy, and threat impact. Warden behavior is modeled via an adaptive attack-selection process capturing detection-triggered escalation and nonstationary strategies. We propose Cross-Domain Factorized Adaptive Lifelong Learning with Proximal Policy Opti- mization (CDFALL-PPO), which factorizes shared and domain-specific policy components for online adaptation while mitigating catastrophic forgetting. Across three escalating 30-task sequences, extensive simulations show that CDFALL-PPO raises median packet covert delivery rate (PCR) by 14.5 %, increases covert throughput by up to 53.6%, and lowers AoCI by 59.4% relative to PPO. Under the strongest composite attack, mean on-attack PCR improves from 52% to 70%, and mean post-attack recovery PCR rises from 64% to 93%.
item.dc:creator: Yinxuan Wu, Xiaohao Xia, Beatriz Lorenzo, Dennis Goeckel, Fikadu Dagefu

item.title: Beyond Raw IQ: Compact Semantic Representations for Task Oriented Automatic Modulation Classification
item.description: arXiv:2611.28813v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automatic modulation classification (AMC) is an important component of modern wireless communication systems, but conventional signal representations can be expensive to store, process, and communicate, particularly under noisy channel conditions. This work investigates whether learned semantic representations can provide a compact alternative to high-dimensional in-phase and quadrature (IQ) representations while retaining robustness to noise. Starting from a 2048-dimensional IQ representation, we evaluate learned semantic representations with dimensions of 4, 8, 16, 32, and 64. Across the evaluated configurations, a 16-dimensional representation provides the strongest overall trade-off between classification performance, robustness, and representation size. The resulting representation achieves a 128x compression ratio and a 99.22% reduction in dimensionality. We further evaluate representation stability across signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs), compare semantic representations with a raw-IQ CNN, analyze per-class robustness, and perform five-seed validation. The five-seed evaluation produces an average accuracy of (49.22 +- 0.52)% and Macro-F1 of (49.27 +- 0.53)% across the evaluated SNR range. These results indicate that learned semantic compression can produce a substan- tially smaller representation while preserving useful classification information and improving geometric stability under noise.
item.dc:creator: Omm Swarup, Shrishail M. Hiremath

item.title: Handover Cost Optimization in LEO Satellite Networks using an RL-based Multiple-Column Selection Strategy via Branch-and-Price
item.description: arXiv:2611.29129v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Next-generation wireless networks increasingly rely on low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites for broad coverage and low latency, making efficient handover management essential. We formulate satellite handover as a combinatorial optimization problem, assigning each ground user to exactly one capacity-limited, visible satellite while minimizing network handover costs. We propose a reinforcement learning (RL)-based branch-and-price (B&P) framework with learned multiple-column selection (MCS) to accelerate column generation while retaining exact dynamic programming pricing. We also develop two lightweight heuristic policies: handover-aware visibility duration (HAVD) for online decisions and congestion-aware predictive (CAP) for offline planning. Additionally, a local-search repair algorithm adapts precomputed B&P or MCS-B&P solutions to demand perturbations through single-flip and per-user trajectory re-optimization, avoiding complete re-optimization. Simulations using realistic large scale constellations, including Starlink Gen-1, demonstrate that MCS-B&P achieves solution quality comparable to exact B&P with fewer column-generation iterations, fewer branch-and-bound nodes, and reduced computation time. HAVD and CAP offer effective online and offline cost-latency trade-offs, while local-search repair recovers most performance losses due to demand perturbations at a fraction of the computational cost of full re-optimization.
item.dc:creator: Mandar R. Nalavade, Gaurav S. Kasbekar, Koushik Kar

item.title: Exploiting Queue Information for Quality of Services Routing in SDN Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.29385v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Routing costs determine how deterministic networks allocate feasible queue resources to successive flow requests. We propose a topology-aware cost that combines normalized network-calculus post-admission delay and backlog bounds with static path diversity and shortest-path load concentration. Their product weights the backlog premium above a delay baseline within a shared queue-level routing, LARAC, and admission-control framework. Across ten paired runs, the proposed cost admits 657.7, 478.9, and 168.2 more flows than Max-Risk on Polska, NSFNET, and COST266, respectively; the corresponding 95% confidence intervals exclude zero. Germany50 shows a smaller gain of 67.6 flows with an interval crossing zero. The proposed cost has the highest mean acceptance among five costs on three of the four topologies. Gains are accompanied by comparable or lower mean hop counts and cannot be explained simply by higher aggregate utilization. On 100-1000-node networks, risk-aware costs remain comparatively stable while delay-only acceptance declines. A centralized SDN realization reduces distributed control and protocol-state overhead, while large-scale results expose the associated routing-performance tradeoff.
item.dc:creator: Hong-Li Lin, Yung-Chung Wang

item.title: Two Rounds Are Already Hard for Loop-Free Updates of Routing Trees
item.description: arXiv:2611.29695v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Updating a routing tree can create loops even when the old and new trees lead to the same destination. A controller chooses which routers update in each round, but their updates may finish in any order. Strong loop freedom therefore requires every partial completion to be acyclic. We show that deciding whether two rounds suffice is NP-complete, even when a safe three-round schedule is supplied. The proof is a linear-size reduction from 3-SAT with one old clause spine and four routers per variable. Three types of mixed cycles enforce consistent literal choices and clause satisfaction. For every nonempty input formula, the constructed instance needs exactly two rounds if the formula is satisfiable and exactly three otherwise.
item.dc:creator: Klaus-Tycho Foerster

item.title: Scheduling Algorithms for Millimeter-Wave Full-Duplex Integrated Access and Backhaul
item.description: arXiv:2611.29708v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Integrated access and backhaul (IAB) is a cost-effective way to deploy millimeter-wave cellular networks, but under half-duplex (HD) operation, it exhibits poor latency and throughput scaling, as an IAB node's panels are typically scheduled to either all transmit or all receive in a given time slot to avoid self-interference. Upgrading IAB nodes with full-duplex capability (FD) allows their panels to be scheduled more flexibly, but doing so optimally across an entire network is challenging since self-interference couples link rates with scheduling decisions across nodes. In this work, we first develop a distributed dynamic programming algorithm that resolves this coupling by passing messages up and down the IAB tree, computing throughput-optimal back-pressure schedules in near-linear time. To reduce the control overhead associated with this approach, we also propose Floor-based Reduced-Overhead MaxWeight (FROM), which instead allows each node to schedule its panels independently of how its child nodes are scheduled. FROM accomplishes this by computing a floor on outgoing backhaul rates and scheduling each node using only local queue and channel states and its parent node's decision. We characterize the downlink stability region of this class of reduced-overhead policies and show that it spans at least half of the global stability region. We further prove that FROM stabilizes a guaranteed fraction of this region and identify conditions under which it achieves throughput optimality. Numerical results show that full-duplex IAB networks support higher traffic loads and lower delay than conventional half-duplex ones, and that FROM approaches the performance of global scheduling, even outperforming it when accounting for control overhead.
item.dc:creator: Sungho Cho, Changhee Joo, Ian P. Roberts

item.title: Occamy: A Semi-Oblivious Reconfigurable Datacenter Network
item.description: arXiv:2611.29714v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reconfigurable datacenter networks use fast circuit switches to provide high bandwidth at low cost, thereby emerging as a compelling alternative to packet switching. However, existing designs either react to fine-grained demand, requiring frequent optimization across the network, or remain completely demand-oblivious, requiring all-to-all connectivity that limits the cost benefits of circuit switching. We present Occamy, a semi-oblivious reconfigurable datacenter network that implements a tunable level of demand-fitting: it aggregates nodes into tunable-size clusters, and adapts a node-level circuit schedule to the coarse-grained demand between these clusters, thereby leveraging a demand-aware topology without frequent optimization overhead. Results on traditional cloud workloads and an AI training workload show that Occamy significantly improves the cost-performance tradeoff over state-of-the-art oblivious and demand-aware circuit-switched designs, while maintaining low overhead. We demonstrate the practicality of our approach using existing circuit-switched technology, implement an FPGA-based prototype, and evaluate failures.
item.dc:creator: Nitika Saran, Keting Chen, Yunxi Shen, Daniel Amir, Tegan Wilson, Robert Kleinberg, Vishal Shrivastav, Hakim Weatherspoon

item.title: A Reactive Cross-Layer QoS Adaptation Framework for SDN-Enabled DDS Communications in IoD
item.description: arXiv:2611.30223v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Internet of Drones (IoD) is a subset of the Internet of Things (IoT) where drones operate as networked smart objects communicating with entities across terrestrial, aerial, and spatial domains. The increasing deployment of drones has accelerated the adoption of IoD in both mainstream and emerging applications. Increasingly, IoD systems rely on the standardized Data Distribution Service (DDS) as their communication middleware, thanks to its rich Quality of Service (QoS) policies, which enable meeting the demanding constraints of IoD applications. However, QoS policies, particularly reliability modes, are often statically configured, which limits their effectiveness in IoD environments that are characterized by high mobility, frequent network impairments, and dynamic topology changes. In this paper, we propose a reactive QoS adaptation framework for DDS-based IoD systems. The framework leverages Software Defined Networking (SDN) to capture global network conditions and incorporates device energy levels and topic popularity to dynamically adapt reliability modes to changing operating environments. By jointly considering network-level, device-level, and topic-level inputs, the proposed approach enhances middleware adaptability, reliability, and efficiency. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework compared to static QoS configurations.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Ali Zormati, Ghada Jaber, Hicham Lakhlef

item.title: Fetch, Read, Reuse: How AI Search Agents Bend the Web's Rules
item.description: arXiv:2611.30546v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI search agents form a new and fast-growing class of web traffic. Like a browser, they fetch pages on demand for one user; like a transcoding proxy, they rewrite what they fetch; and like a shared cache, they answer other users' questions from the stored copy. The rules publishers rely on, such as robots.txt, Retry-After, and Cache-Control, were written for more familiar clients, so the agent's vendor decides which of them to follow. We present a black-box measurement study of how these agents fetch, read, and reuse pages, covering the search APIs of OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI, and Google and the consumer apps of ten services. We find that OpenAI and xAI do not honor robots.txt, and no service acts on Retry-After. Services silently read less than the origin served: OpenAI drops some formats, no service reads JavaScript-only content, and xAI reads only the first 0.5 MB of a page. OpenAI, Anthropic, and xAI share fetched pages across users and largely ignore Cache-Control, so answers can reflect outdated pages for 30 minutes to a day or more. Publishers therefore lack effective control: directives are advisory and followed selectively, describe the served page rather than the rewritten copy, and bound how long a copy is reused but not how many answers it serves. We release our code and data.
item.dc:creator: Yixi Chen, Zafar A. Qazi, Marco Canini, Suhaib A. Fahmy

item.title: Stress2Twin: Profile-Driven Network Digital Twins for Guarded Edge Computing Resource Management
item.description: arXiv:2611.30699v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Heterogeneous edge systems require resource managers to determine how many application replicas to deploy, where to place them, and how to distribute incoming requests while satisfying service-level performance constraints. Acquiring the performance knowledge required for these decisions through exhaustive multi-node characterization is measurement-intensive and becomes increasingly difficult as the number of workers and configurations grows. Stress2Twin is a profile-driven Network Digital Twin (NDT) framework that profiles edge nodes independently and composes their measured behavior into a system-level resource-management model. Machine-level oracles characterize latency, throughput, loss, queueing, and power as functions of assigned request rate and replica count. A guarded optimizer derives operating regions and tests neighboring request-rate states before retaining a replica count, reserving capacity before measured nonlinear degradation. Independent profiling of our three-worker Kubernetes testbed requires 271 measured states, corresponding to approximately 4.5 hours, compared with an estimated 123 hours for exhaustive characterization of the considered cluster configuration space. In a single-run ramp evaluation, the selected policy records no latency or loss-threshold violations within the derived 1,650 requests per second (RPS) supported range and reduces estimated power by 27.84% relative to RPS100 Round Robin (RR) placement. An additional single-run evaluation under a non-monotonic workload records no latency violation and 19.67% lower estimated energy than a stabilized RPS50 RR policy. These results show that independently acquired machine profiles can support capacity-aware resource consolidation within a measured operating range. Power savings use an idealized active-worker accounting model.
item.dc:creator: Julian Jimenez-Agudelo, Paola Soto, Ayat Zaki-Hindi, S\'ebastien Faye, Nina Slamnik-Krije\v{s}torac, Johann Marquez-Barja, Miguel Camelo-Botero

item.title: Connected but Late: Sample Age of Commercial BLE Wearables under Wi-Fi Coexistence for Real-Time Clinical Applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.30774v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wearable sensors are increasingly being used in real-time clinical applications, such as rehabilitation robots and live therapy monitoring. As Healthcare 5.0 moves towards personalized therapies, their use will continue growing, potentially compromising communication reliability. Most wearables transmit over Bluetooth Low Energy, sharing 2.4 GHz with institutional Wi-Fi. Previous coexistence studies have focused on whether data arrive, rather than when. We measured sample age for a commercial electrocardiogram strap, from acquisition through the gateway to storage in our platform MEDWEAR, in an anechoic chamber and a hospital rehabilitation gym, and we compared it with illustrative clinical deadlines. Without load, the strap's own framing was the largest source of delay, making samples on average 280 ms and up to 550 ms old before transmission. Wi-Fi load had no measurable effect while adaptive frequency hopping could avoid the loaded channel. In a stress test, which forced the link onto the loaded channel, the link became the dominant source of delay, adding up to 11 s. The link stayed connected, but a median of 29% of samples and up to 98% (worst case) were older than 1 s on arrival at the gateway. The gym behaved mostly like the quiet chamber, but during one traffic burst, while hopping was restricted, up to 4.6% of samples were older than 1 s. These results show that a connected link can deliver late data. Therefore, sensors intended for real-time clinical applications should be profiled in situ and monitored based on sample age rather than connection status alone.
item.dc:creator: Monica Perez-Serrano, H\"umay Zehra \"Ozer, Seung Ju Paek, Diego Paez-Granados

item.title: Geometry, Reliability, and Spacetime Dynamics of Hyper-Simplex Fractal Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.31161v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large-scale, delay-tolerant peer-to-peer networks that need strong consistency usually separate naming, routing, consensus, and ordering into independent layers. To bring deterministic network properties into complex peer-to-peer structures, we unify all four on a single recursive topology. Modeling mutual equality among N peers in Euclidean space requires dimension at least N-1, which prevents flat equal groups from scaling at fixed dimension. The hyper-simplex fractal network G(N,m) escapes this limit by recursion. Each non-leaf node anchors a half-scale N-clique. From the resulting digit-word addresses alone, nodes decide adjacency without routing tables, forward greedily along exact shortest paths, and converge geometrically to a self-similar attractor of dimension log_2 N. Running hierarchical PBFT on the same prefix tree achieves linear message load and logarithmic fault-free latency, with an explicit reliability threshold under independent faults and analytical recursions for anchor exposure, dual homing, and event registration. Reversible topology edits generate the Higman-Thompson group V_N on the address boundary, block order characterizes service-topology hosting beyond treewidth, and root-anchored block heights yield persistent spacetime coordinates with compact light-client proofs.
item.dc:creator: Hao Xu, Kaiwen Yang, Jiacheng Qian, Yinuo Liu, Chih-Lin I

item.title: Schism: Reconfigurable Scale-Up Domains for Distributed Quantum Computing
item.description: arXiv:2611.31193v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Switch-based quantum datacenters connect quantum processing units (QPUs) through photonic switches and shared Bell-state measurement (BSM) devices. Sharing BSMs saves hardware, but fixed connectivity constrains access to these resources. Local communication can overload one rack's BSMs while others remain idle; reaching those idle resources incurs additional optical loss and retries through switches and quantum frequency converters (QFCs). Programs remain locked into this locality-contention tradeoff as their communication patterns change. We propose Schism, an architecture that lets programs dynamically change which QPUs share each BSM pool. Schism places BSM pools at aggregation switches and QFCs on their core-facing uplinks. Top-of-rack switches establish reconfigurable native-wavelength circuits from QPUs to these pools, forming scale-up domains bounded by the optical loss budget. Reconfiguration reshapes resource sharing across racks without moving QPUs or migrating quantum states. Our key insight is that QPU grouping jointly determines photon-path loss and contention for BSM resources: locality alone cannot identify the best grouping, and a grouping pays off only if its savings outweigh the delay of reconfiguring to it. We develop an optimization framework that combines graph partitioning with resource-constrained completion-time estimates and dynamic programming to select how QPUs share BSM pools and when those groupings reconfigure, between or within circuit phases. Our evaluation using SeQUeNCe with trapped-ion parameters shows that Schism achieves communication speedups of 4.9-7.3x across 11 workloads on 32 QPUs compared to Fixed Clos connectivity and 3.6-8.3x compared to SwitchQNet. Schism also outperforms a hypothetical network-wide switch by 1.35-1.38x on the eight workloads whose phases fit in a pool, and trails it by 1.1-1.75x on the other three.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Alexander, Deeksha P Rao, Nilesh Vyas, Vamsi Addanki

item.title: Robust Trajectory Prediction Under Sensing and V2X Noise: Evaluation and Mitigation Strategies
item.description: arXiv:2611.28128v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Anticipating the future behavior of surrounding objects is key for the safe and efficient navigation of autonomous vehicles. State-of-the-art Transformer-based interaction-aware trajectory prediction models are typically trained and evaluated on large-scale, highly curated datasets obtained by filtering any object detection and tracking noise through extensive offline post-processing. However, in real-world deployments, the detected objects' state (position, heading, and speed) estimates are inherently affected by sensing and localization uncertainties. These uncertainties can be even higher for connected and automated vehicles receiving information from other road users through Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communications. In this paper, we first investigate the sensitivity of five state-of-the-art Transformer-based interaction-aware trajectory prediction models to realistic noisy object state estimates. Numerical results show that prediction accuracy degrades by up to a 6x factor as the noise level increases, highlighting the models' sensitivity to the mismatch between the noise conditions encountered during training and those experienced at deployment. We then show that retraining models on a more realistic noise-augmented dataset is a more effective strategy to mitigate the impact of noisy object state estimates on trajectory prediction accuracy than using denoising modules at the input. Retrained models limit the prediction accuracy degradation below a 1.5x factor. The noise-augmented dataset is openly released to support further research.
item.dc:creator: Shahab Salehi, Luca Lusvarghi, Miguel Sepulcre, Javier Gozalvez

item.title: Online Scheduling for Entanglement Distillation: Learning When to Wait
item.description: arXiv:2611.28373v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Entanglement distillation probabilistically increases the fidelity of entangled pairs at the cost of reducing their number. The outcome of each distillation operation takes time to communicate, during which the entangled pairs decohere while idle in their memories. This raises a dilemma: wait for the outcome before proceeding, or continue optimistically at the risk of needlessly consuming further pairs. We study online distillation scheduling, in which distillation trees are constructed dynamically to maximize the throughput of pairs that meet a required fidelity. A policy decides which pairs to distill together and, for each operation, whether to wait for its outcome. We derive an upper bound on the throughput of every scheduling policy and, by formulating the problem as a Markov decision process, train, with reinforcement learning, a policy that applies to any number of memories. Compared with two baselines that always or never wait, the learned policy delivers as many pairs of the required fidelity as the better one when one of these two extremes is the best choice, and more otherwise.
item.dc:creator: Panagiotis Promponas, Spyros Tserkis, Leandros Tassiulas

item.title: RadioWorld: Transferring World Models to Radio-Frequency Radiance Fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.29282v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Electromagnetic (EM) wave propagation in the physical world constitutes a Radio-Frequency (RF) radiance field, providing rich information for 6G communication and sensing. However, existing neural RF field methods suffer from three fundamental limitations: (1) they predominantly rely on per-scene optimization and cannot generalize to unseen scenes; (2) they require costly reference RF measurements in each target scene; and (3) they degrade severely when extrapolating beyond the vicinity of reference measurements. To overcome these limitations, we present RadioWorld, a general framework that adapts a world model to synthesize RF radiance fields directly from physical scene geometry and transceiver locations, without requiring any reference RF measurements at inference. Specifically, RadioWorld couples two specialized modules within a dual-stream Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) architecture: a Scene-Understanding Transformer that encodes 3D scene geometry and transceiver locations to extract environment-aware global EM propagation features, and a Field-Generation Transformer that attends to these features to synthesize the RF radiance field with the local query conditions. We also establish UrbanRF-Bench, a large-scale ray-traced benchmark spanning 657 urban scenes and 32,850 RF radiance fields across seven global cities. Extensive experiments demonstrate that RadioWorld significantly outperforms specialized baselines and accurately synthesizes RF fields at arbitrary locations in unseen cities. Code, datasets, and checkpoints will be released upon acceptance.
item.dc:creator: Hu Zhou, Jiazhou Zhou, Shuowen Zhang, Ying-Chang Liang, Liang Liu

item.title: Mitigating Nested GTP Attacks: A Closed-Loop eBPF Defense for 5G and Beyond Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.29756v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The evolving cellular networks continue to rely on the legacy GPRS Tunneling Protocol-User Plane (GTP-U) to encapsulate and route user data traffic across the data plane. Recent security research demonstrated that nested GTP-U (GTP-in-GTP) payload vulnerabilities enable a diverse range of attacks on victim users. To address this vulnerability, in this paper, we propose a closed-loop extended Berkeley Packet Filter (eBPF) and eXpress Data Path (XDP) defense to detect and mitigate nested GTP-U attacks in 5G and beyond networks. The proposed framework contains three components: an in-kernel XDP Detection and Drop Module (XDP-DDM), a user-space User-Plane Telemetry Agent (UP-TA), and a multi-threaded Control-Plane Mitigation Orchestrator (CP-MO). We implement and evaluate the proposed defense on a sliced 5G testbed integrating Free5GC, UERANSIM, and Containerlab. Experimental results indicate that the XDP-DDM detects and drops malicious nested GTP-U packets at line rate, while the UP-TA and CP-MO asynchronously report and revoke the attacker's network access, respectively. Under a 10,000 packets-per-second cross-slice nested GTP-U flood, the proposed solution preserves the baseline performance of the victim slices while introducing minimal overhead. We also show that the proposed solution has minimal impact on the user's throughput and round-trip time.
item.dc:creator: AbdulAziz AbdulGhaffar, Ashraf Matrawy

item.title: Closed-Form Formula for $d_{\mathrm{critical}}(a_0)$ in Large Fully Connected Power Grids
item.description: arXiv:2611.30922v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Kadloor and Santhi (arXiv:1011.4098) modeled cascading failures in a large fully connected power grid by a coupled four-variable recursion for the minimum surviving load $a_n$, the mean failed load $\mu_{n-1}$, the redistributed load $\mathcal{D}_n$, and the stagewise failure probability $p_n$. They noted that the recursion was not tractable and identified the critical disturbance $d_{\mathrm{critical}}$ by simulation. We show that the recursion telescopes exactly into a one-dimensional monotone map $a_{n+1} = g(a_n)$. This yields the threshold in closed form: $1 - a_0 = d_{\mathrm{critical}}\,(1 + \ln(1 + 1/d_{\mathrm{critical}}))$, or explicitly in terms of the lower branch $W_{-1}$ of the Lambert W function. We prove a sharp dichotomy. For $d_m \le d_{\mathrm{critical}}$ the cascade halts with limiting load $a_0 + d_{\mathrm{critical}}$ at criticality and surviving fraction $1/(1 + d_{\mathrm{critical}})$. For $d_m > d_{\mathrm{critical}}$ a complete outage occurs in finitely many steps.
item.dc:creator: Sachin Kadloor

item.title: Industrial Viewpoints on RAN Technologies for 6G
item.description: arXiv:2508.08225v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Sixth-generation (6G) mobile systems have entered the standardization phase, with commercial deployments anticipated around 2030. This article presents an industrial perspective on the performance targets and key technologies shaping the 6G radio access network (RAN). It examines advances in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO), artificial intelligence (AI), waveforms, channel coding, signal constellations, integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), and the integration of terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks (NTNs). Although detailed specification work is still ahead, the scope of the 6G studies has been defined and substantial technical progress has been made. We assess the emerging technologies and design choices from the perspectives of implementation complexity, computational and energy efficiency, interoperability, deployment feasibility, and migration from 5G. By connecting research advances with practical standardization and commercialization considerations, this article aims to inform researchers and industry practitioners developing the 6G RAN.
item.dc:creator: Mansoor Shafi, Erik G. Larsson, Xingqin Lin, Dorin Panaitopol, Stefan Parkvall, Flavien Ronteix-Jacquet, Antti Toskala

item.title: Carbon-Aware Age of Information Scheduling in IoT Networks
item.description: arXiv:2605.21328v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Ensuring timely information delivery while reducing environmental impact is a fundamental challenge in future large-scale 6G and beyond Internet of Things (IoT) deployments. Information timeliness is typically measured using the Age of Information (AoI) metric, whereas environmental impact is often characterized by the Carbon Footprint (CF), which depends on both energy consumption and the Carbon Intensity (CI), defined as the amount of CO$_2$-equivalent emissions produced per unit of consumed energy. Because CI varies over time, minimizing energy consumption alone does not necessarily minimize CF: transmitting the same status update at different times may result in different carbon costs. To address this challenge, we propose Sustainable Age-of-Information Scheduling for IoT Hardware-Constrained Edge Networks (SAOITHE), a scalable scheduling heuristic inspired by Whittle-index decomposition. A closed-form index is derived for a relaxed infinite-horizon single-source model with immediate transmission and unit AoI reset; this index is subsequently used as a priority rule for the original finite-horizon, multi-source system with buffered gateway and server dynamics. Using real-world CI traces across low-, medium-, and high-CI regions, the proposed heuristic operates within the allocated CF and duty-cycle budgets in all evaluated configurations and achieves lower average AoI than baseline policies. The AoI reduction relative to Round Robin is approximately 25% and 20% in low- and medium-CI regions, respectively, and up to 75% in high-CI settings, while maintaining quasilinear per-slot computational complexity.
item.dc:creator: Shih-Kai Chou, Maice Costa, Mihael Mohor\v{c}i\v{c}, Jernej Hribar

item.title: Online Stochastic Matchings: Stability on Hypergraphs
item.description: arXiv:2607.18935v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In stochastic dynamic matching, items of several classes arrive at rates $\lambda$ and leave in compatible groups. When groups may exceed two items, as in quantum switches or organ exchange, compatibility is described by the incidence matrix $A$ of a hypergraph, whose entries count how many items of each class a group consumes (single-class hyperedges can model discards). We call a system stabilizable if some matching policy keeps large queues rare in the long run, and show that this holds if and only if the conservation equation $A\mu = \lambda$ admits a nonnegative solution whose support induces a surjective submatrix. Equivalently, $\lambda$ lies in the interior of the cone generated by the hyperedges. The condition is necessary for all policies, including idling and clairvoyant ones. It is sufficient through one explicit policy: the rewardless counterpart of the Extended Greedy Primal--Dual policy of Nazari and Stolyar (2019) stabilizes every stabilizable system without knowledge of the rates, and its mean queue length is explicitly bounded. Approaching a solution whose support is not surjective has a cost, under every policy: matching rates within $\epsilon$ of it force mean queues of order at least $1/\epsilon$. On simple graphs, some greedy policies stabilize every stabilizable system. On a small hypergraph with a single hyperedge of size three, every greedy policy is unstable on an open set of stabilizable rates. This shows that no greedy policy, nor any family of greedy policies, can approach maximal stability on hypergraphs: idling is necessary. We also settle two cases explicitly: the complete $k$-uniform hypergraph (the $k$-partite quantum switch), which is stabilizable exactly when no link generates a fraction $1/k$ or more of the total rate, and the Fano plane.
item.dc:creator: Fabien Mathieu (NPA)

item.title: The LQ Digital Mode Family: Protocol Architecture and Reference Specification for Weak-Signal Communications
item.description: arXiv:2609.06427v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper introduces LQ8, an open-source weak-signal digital mode for amateur radio that completes structured two-way contacts in 4 transmissions (60 s), achieving a 1.50x speedup over canonical 6-transmission exchanges (90 s) and 1.25x over 5-transmission RR73 exchanges (75 s) while preserving complete bidirectional exchange of Maidenhead grid locators, signal reports, and mutual acknowledgments. By replacing fixed-width message-type headers with variable-length prefix codes matched to physical-layer bit budgets, LQ8 packs the answering station's grid locator and measured signal report into a single 77-bit reply. In multi-station pileup operations, LQ8 confirms up to two answering stations simultaneously within a single-carrier 50.0 Hz transmission with a 0.0 dB RF power-splitting penalty, achieving a peak rate of 240 QSOs/h in continuous pileup (4x over single-carrier FT8; 480 QSOs/h dual-carrier) while retaining -21.0 dB SNR sensitivity. The protocol family also defines three extended profiles (LQ16, LQ4, and LQ2) tailored for extreme sensitivity, VHF/UHF contesting, and fast-burst channels.
item.dc:creator: Luis Quesada

item.title: FLoRa: Flight-Assisted Data Collection from Duty Cycling LoRa Nodes under Energy Constraints
item.description: arXiv:2610.09226v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Data collection using Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) is challenging when LoRa IoT Devices (IoTDs) duty-cycle to conserve battery. Under energy constraints, a UAV must decide which IoTDs to visit, in what order, where to hover, and how many times to probe each node, while time-based data freshness decays. Tractably solving this problem requires a multi-level optimization architecture: discrete combinatorial optimization for routing, continuous global optimization for spatial positioning, and sequential decision-making under uncertainty. We propose FLoRa, a Flight-assisted LoRa data collection architecture using Simulated Annealing (SA) for path planning, Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy (CMA-ES) for hover positioning, and Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes (POMDPs) for probing IoTDs. To quantify collection utility from duty-cycling nodes, we introduce the Value of Information for Pull-based systems (VIP), a metric that rewards fresh data and penalizes failed probes, imposing well-posedness and preventing indefinite probing when an IoTD is off. Tracking hard battery constraints on every POMDP sample path requires state augmentation, worsening the curse of dimensionality. For tractability, SA and CMA-ES work on the hard battery constraints, while at the POMDP layer we relax them into soft average constraints via Lagrangian relaxation. Since solving the network-wide POMDP is computationally complex, we decompose it into node-level POMDPs by approximating inter-node time dependency using a forward-decomposition technique. Evaluation shows that FLoRa outperforms greedy, metaheuristic, and deep reinforcement learning baselines, as well as recent UAV data collection methods, by 27.8-76.1% in total expected VIP, 23.5-45.7% in node coverage, and 23.3-54.4% in successful collections.
item.dc:creator: Naresh Babu Kakarla, V. Mahendran

item.title: Communication-Aware Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Decentralized Cooperative UAV Deployment
item.description: arXiv:2603.16141v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Autonomous Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) swarms are increasingly used as rapidly deployable aerial relays and sensing platforms, yet practical deployments must operate under partial observability and intermittent peer-to-peer connectivity. We present a graph-based multi-agent reinforcement learning framework trained under centralized training with decentralized execution (CTDE): a centralized critic and global state are available only during training, while each UAV executes a shared policy using local observations and messages from nearby neighbors. Under restricted communication, neighbor relations are induced by an SNR-threshold connectivity graph. Our architecture encodes local agent state and nearby entities with an agent-entity attention module and aggregates inter-UAV messages with neighbor self-attention over a signal-quality-limited communication graph defined by a channel model. We evaluate the framework on a cooperative relay-deployment task, DroneConnect. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves an approximately 12% increase in target coverage over MAPPO under restricted communication and partial observability, while remaining competitive with a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP)-based offline upper bound with full node observability.
item.dc:creator: Enguang Fan, Zihan Shan, Yifan Chen, Klara Nahrstedt, Matthew Caesar, Jae Kim

item.title: Neilson's Weak vs. Strong Loss Aversion: A Characterization and a Generalized CPT-Utility Function
item.description: arXiv:2607.22085v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In multi-objective and multi-criteria decision-making under risk, especially in settings involving individual behavior, risk-aware analysis based on subjective evaluation has become increasingly important. Moving beyond risk-neutral modeling and the constraints of Expected Utility Theory (EUT), Cumulative Prospect Theory (CPT) provides a behaviorally grounded framework for capturing how individuals perceive and evaluate risky prospects. This paper conducts a rigorous theoretical analysis of Neilson's definitions of aversion. We provide a gamble-based interpretation, sharpen key conceptual distinctions, and make explicit the conditions under which the weak and strong notions coincide as well as when they diverge. Furthermore, we examine the Kobberling-Wakker utility function and related standard CPT specifications, highlighting structural limitations and inconsistencies that arise when these forms are required to satisfy Neilson-type aversion conditions. To address these issues, we propose a generalized CPT-utility function that retains the canonical reference-dependent shape while offering additional flexibility. This generalization extends the descriptive scope of CPT and provides an explicit functional form that is useful for sensitivity analysis and utility function-based optimization.
item.dc:creator: Symeon Vaidanis, Marios Kountouris

item.title: Physiological Information Reliability: Contextual-Bandit Allocation of Coding Redundancy and Computation in Multimodal Cardiovascular Sensing
item.description: arXiv:2609.00435v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A packet can arrive intact and still be nearly worthless. On a body-worn node the radio and processor share one small battery, yet ECG and photoplethysmography (PPG) windows differ widely in how much an estimator can recover from them. We propose Physiological Information Reliability (PIR): a hand-designed window-value proxy, PIV, built from signal quality and cross-modal heart-rate agreement, joins channel, energy and compute telemetry in one state vector, and a LinUCB bandit chooses coding redundancy and processing site. Over 25 paired seeds on a synthetic burst-erasure testbed, PIR-LinUCB used 4.3% less energy than a hand-written rule, with lower error and higher delivery. A rule that also reads PIV matches it on error and delivery but spends 3.7 mJ more per window. On five real fetal ECG recordings, PIV tracked heart-rate error better than signal quality alone (mean within-record Spearman $\rho = -0.50$ against $-0.40$). The evidence is simulated, small and non-clinical.
item.dc:creator: Navaneetha Krishnan Kamalakannan, Janakiraman Kamalakannan, Harinisri Velmurugan
